title: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis After Liver Transplant With Oral Vancomycin
official: Preventing Recurrence of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis After Liver Transplant (PROP-LT): a Phase 1, Open-label, Controlled Study of Oral Vancomycin
summary:
Primary Objective:

* To evaluate safety of a 4-week course of oral vancomycin (250 mg 3 times daily \[TID\]) in liver transplant recipients who were transplanted for Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC).

Secondary Objectives:

* To determine tolerability and adherence to a 4-week course of oral vancomycin (250 mg TID) in liver transplant recipients who were transplanted for PSC.
* To assess vancomycin resistant enterococcus (VRE) colonization status over time.
* To assess the impact of oral vancomycin on stool microbiome composition, diversity, and function.
* To assess impact of oral vancomycin on microbial metabolite concentrations in blood and stool.
* To assess impact of oral vancomycin on liver-related biochemical markers.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥ 18 years
* Ability to provide written, informed consent.
* History of orthotopic liver transplantation within 1 to 10 years prior to enrollment (i.e. study drug initiation)
* Diagnosis of PSC as the underlying liver disease leading to liver transplantation, based on compatible imaging findings (magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography \[MRCP\], endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography \[ERCP\], percutaneous transhepatic cholangiogram \[PTC\]), liver histology, and/or clinician judgment
* Subjects with or without IBD may be enrolled. IBD diagnosis with a minimum disease duration of 6 months as assessed by endoscopy/histology. IBD should be in clinical remission or mildly active according to accepted clinical scores and/or clinician judgment.
* Stable liver graft function, as determined by ALL of the following criteria:

  * No episodes of acute rejection within 6 months prior to enrollment, based on liver histology and/or clinical signs or symptoms
  * No episodes of cholangitis within 6 months prior to study enrollment, based on positive bacterial cultures, compatible imaging, and/or clinical signs or symptoms
  * No intervention for biliary obstruction (e.g. ERCP, PTC, surgical intervention) within 6 months prior to study enrollment.
  * Stable liver biochemistries within 6 months prior to study enrollment, as determined by: ALP \<5x ULN
  * Absence of histologic or imaging findings suggestive of cirrhosis

Exclusion Criteria:

* History of colon resection at any time prior to study enrollment or presence of ileal/colonic diversion within 12 months prior to study enrollment
* Documented VRE infection within 12 months prior to study enrollment
* Documented C. difficile infection within 3 months prior to study enrollment
* Systemic antibiotic exposure within 3 months prior to study enrollment
* Change in any transplant or IBD-related immunosuppression or its dosing within 30 days prior to study enrollment
* Currently taking oral vancomycin
* Allergy or intolerance to vancomycin
* Treatment with any investigational drug within 3 months prior to study enrollment
* Severe renal dysfunction (eGFR \<30 mL/min/1.73 m²) or on dialysis
* Any active malignancy
* Pregnant or breastfeeding Page 8
* Any condition that, in the investigator's judgment, would make participation unsafe or interfere with adherence (e.g., severe frailty, uncontrolled psychiatric disease, inability to adhere to TID dosing)
